# 2. Readings

Last week we used estimated coefficients to compute willingness to pay and simulate market shares. But every model we have estimated so far is relatively simple: it assumes everyone in our sample has the same preferences. That is, we only estimate a "fixed parameter" model that reflects the average preferences for the whole sample. In reality, preferences are usually _heterogeneous_ (different people have different preferences).

One way to account for this is to estimate a "mixed" logit model where we assume the preference parameters in our utility models follow some distribution across the sample (usually a normal distribution). Another way is to estimate a fixed parameter model on different sub-groups in our data. Each of these approaches is discussed in this week's video on heterogeneity.

**Take notes** as you watch the video. Throughout the video, I ask practice questions - you should answer those questions as part of your reflection. You may submit your answers however you wish, e.g. type them in your ``r hw_file`` file and / or hand-write them on paper and take a picture. If you take a picture, save it in your ``r hw_dir`` folder, embed it in ``r hw_file`` (e.g. `![](answers.jpg)`), and commit it along with the rest of your work.

Click [here](../content/slides_heterogeneity.pdf) to download the slides in the video as a PDF.
